queries.details:
Extract every insured property location: address, characteristics, valuation, physical attributes. Include locations with 0 units. Never use a loss run.

If a valid property schedule or table containing property rows is present, do not return zero property entries; extract every applicable property row from it.

Use only the sheet or table holding property rows (e.g. 'Locations', 'SOV'); ignore reference/lookup sheets of construction, occupancy, and dropdown codes. Banner rows ('Address', 'COPE', 'Limits and Values') and summary rows ('Totals', 'Row Count') are not properties. A stated row count is a hint only; the actual data rows govern.

Do not extract a property from an ACORD Statement of Values section. If no other property schedule is available, use an ACORD Property Section Premises Information block.

Work down the table one row at a time, from the first data row to the last. Each row is one property: read that row and fill in all of its fields before moving to the next row. Never emit an entry without populating it.

A blank cell in Loc/Bldg, Location Number, Location Name, street address, city, state, ZIP, county, or country means the row repeats the nearest value above it — inherit that value. Blank cells and repeated values are how an SOV writes 'same as above'; they never mark a duplicate row.

5 Loc/Bldg numbers spread across 52 rows means 52 properties. Long runs of similar addresses ('121 Legacy Way', '131 Legacy Way', '141 Legacy Way' ...) and runs of identical addresses (9 rows reading '1251 Dunlap Rd NE') are each separate properties: return one output entry for every source row, even when the Location Number, Location Name, and street address are identical (e.g. 9 rows reading '1251 Dunlap Rd NE' = 9 entries).

Never build the output from distinct Loc/Bldg, Location Number, Location Name, or address values and then search for rows — that inversion drops entries. Before finishing, confirm your entry count equals the number of data rows.

entities.criteria: The property's location identifier; leave blank for new properties. This is not the bldg or loc number
The property's characteristics identifier; leave blank for new properties. This is not the bldg or loc number
Display name / label for the property. If the 'named insured' is a property name (e.g. condominium, housing), use it.
Display name / label for the specific building. Use only when the source explicitly identifies a building name or building label; otherwise leave blank.

The location (site) number for this row — from a 'Loc', 'Loc #', 'Location', 'Location #', or 'Premises #' column, or the LEFT-HAND portion of a combined 'Loc/Bldg' column.

- Compound values: take only the location portion. '2-3', '2.03', '2/3', '2 B', '002-003', 'Loc 2 Bldg 3' all yield '2'. The building portion belongs in Building Number.
- Strip labels and zero padding: 'Loc 4' -> '4', '004' -> '4'.
- In PDFs and Word documents the number often appears once beside a vertically merged cell or group heading spanning many rows. It applies to every row under that heading.
- If the schedule has no location numbering, number the groups sequentially in source order (1, 2, 3 ...), starting a new number wherever a new site or Location Name begins. Do not leave blank when grouping is discernible.
- Not unique. Consecutive rows sharing one value is the normal case.

The building identifier for THIS row — from a 'Bldg', 'Bldg #', 'Building', or 'Building #' column, the RIGHT-HAND portion of a combined 'Loc/Bldg' value ('2-3' -> '3'), or a designator inside the address or Address Line 2 ('144 N Erwin St Bldg 1' -> '1', '# B' -> 'B').

Resolution order, first match wins:
1. An explicit number or letter given for the row.
2. Otherwise, the row's position within its location group: first row is 1, second is 2, and so on, restarting at 1 at each new Location Number. This is the usual case when a schedule has a single 'Loc/Bldg' column populated only on group-opening rows.
3. Blank only when the row has no building — vacant land, 0 buildings.

- Rows sharing one street address are separate buildings and take separate incrementing numbers: 9 rows reading '1251 Dunlap Rd NE' become buildings 1-9 of that location, keeping any letter designators present.
- Strip labels and padding: 'Bldg 07' -> '7'.
- Not unique; values restart at 1 in each location group.
- A 'Number of Bldgs' value greater than 1 never splits a row into multiple entries. That column is a count, not an identifier.
Geographic latitude of the property (−90 to 90)
Geographic longitude of the property (−180 to 180)
Reference ID for the property's street type per definitions API
Directional prefix of the property's street (N., S., E., W.)
Street number of the property

Street name of the property without the street number, directional, type suffix, or unit. Parse it from the full address in the document. E.g., '144 N Erwin St Bldg 1'->'Erwin'; '110-130 Colony Park Ln'->'Colony Park'; '250 Whistle Way'->'Whistle'. Don't leave blank when an address is present.
Unit, suite, or apartment number of the property

The full street address line of the property, including the street number.

- Extract street-number ranges as written: '110-130 Colony Park Ln' stays '110-130 Colony Park Ln'.
- This is the street address only. Never substitute a location name, building name, or Loc/Bldg number.
- Do not output placeholders or non-addresses: 'See SOV', 'Various', 'TBD', 'Same as above', blank-equivalents.
- Not unique. Two or more entries legitimately carry identical address text when a site has multiple buildings, or when one building's units are listed on separate rows and distinguished only by Street Address 2, Unit Number, building value, or unit count.
data_validation_rules: A row with a blank street address but populated value, unit, or characteristic cells is a distinct property. Output it with the address inherited from the row above.
Addresses differing by any character — street number, unit, or building designator — are separate properties. 118, 116, 140, 130, 111, and 121 on the same street are six properties, not one.
Remove a bare address entry only when it carries no data of its own and every value on it is already represented by more specific building or unit entries at that address.

entities.criteria: Street address line 2 of the property
City of the property. If the city cell is blank due to merged or repeated table values, inherit the applicable city from the nearest row above.
County of the property
Two-letter state code of the property. If the state cell is blank due to merged or repeated table values, inherit the applicable state from the nearest row above.
5-digit or ZIP+4 postal code of the property. If the ZIP cell is blank due to merged or repeated table values, inherit the applicable ZIP from the nearest row above.
Country name of the property
Formatted first line of the property's address for display
Formatted second line of the property's address (City, State ZIP)
Whether the property's address has been verified (true/false)
Whether the property is excluded from the submission (true/false)

Output ONLY the exact Name string for the property's use (not the description, not an ID). Must be one of these 12 values exactly (punctuation and capitalization):
'Residential Habitational' — apartments/multi-family rentals
'Residential Habitational-SFD DPLX' — single-family dwellings or duplexes
'Residential Condominium/HOA' — residential condo associations/HOAs
'Mixed Tenancy Mixed Use - Hab' — mixed-use, primarily residential rental
'Mixed Tenancy Mixed Use - Condo' — mixed-use, condo-owned
'Industrial Commercial/Office' — offices
'Industrial Commercial/Retail' — stores/shopping centers
'Industrial Commercial/Industrial' — manufacturing/industrial
'Industrial Commercial/Warehouse' — warehouses/distribution
'Industrial Commercial Storage Units' — self-storage
'Industrial Parking Lot/Structure' — parking
'Industrial Vacant Land' — undeveloped land
If uncertain between residential options, default to 'Residential Habitational'.

Identify the property's ISO construction class and output ONE value below, character-for-character, with nothing else — no ID, no explanation, no quotes:
ISO 1 - Wood Frame
ISO 2 - Joisted Masonry
ISO 3 - Noncombustible
ISO 4 - Masonry Noncombustible
ISO 5 - Modified Fire Resistive
ISO 6 - Fire Resistive
Not Available

Decision procedure, stop at the first step that resolves:
1. The source names an ISO class number or class name -> output that value.
2. A fire-resistance rating is stated for the frame or floors: 2 hours or more -> ISO 6; 1 hour to under 2 hours -> ISO 5.
3. Classify by materials:
- Combustible exterior walls (wood framing; veneer or stucco over wood), any floors/roof -> ISO 1
- Masonry/brick/block/concrete walls WITH combustible floors or roof (wood joists, wood deck) -> ISO 2
- Masonry/brick/block/concrete walls WITH noncombustible floors and roof (steel deck, concrete, tilt-up) -> ISO 4
- Unprotected metal or steel walls, floors, and supports, all noncombustible -> ISO 3
4. Otherwise -> Not Available

Source-term mapping: frame, wood joist, brick/stone veneer, stucco on frame, EIFS over wood -> ISO 1. Joisted masonry, ordinary construction, brick joisted, masonry/frame, mill, heavy timber with masonry walls -> ISO 2. Noncombustible, all-metal, pre-engineered metal, unprotected steel frame -> ISO 3. Masonry noncombustible, concrete tilt-up, block with steel deck, CBS with metal roof -> ISO 4. Modified fire resistive, protected steel or reinforced concrete rated 1-2 hours -> ISO 5. Fire resistive, protected structural steel, poured/reinforced concrete rated 2+ hours -> ISO 6.

Constraints: classify only from explicit statements about materials, wall/floor/roof composition, or fire rating. Never infer from age, year built, occupancy, tenant, square footage, stories, location, or premium. Masonry walls with no floor/roof information -> Not Available. 'Steel' with no protection or rating -> Not Available. Conflicting or unattributable values -> Not Available. When uncertain between two classes -> Not Available.

Extract the Sprinkler Type ID and return exactly one of these values: `None`, `Parking Only`, `Partial`, or `Full`. Use `None` when no sprinkler system is present, `Parking Only` when sprinklers cover only the parking area, `Partial` when coverage is above 0% but below 100%, and `Full` when coverage is 100% **or the document states that all buildings or structures at the property are sprinklered.
data_validation_rules: Never return null; return the literal word `None`.

entities.criteria:
Output ONLY the exact value string for the property's housing type (not the description, not an ID). Must be one of these values exactly (punctuation and capitalization):
'Assisted Living' — assisted living, memory care, or residents receiving daily living support
'Nursing Home' — skilled nursing, convalescent, or long-term medical care facilities
'Senior' — age-restricted (55+/62+) or independent senior living communities without medical/assistance services
'Student' — student housing, dormitories, or properties marketed to university students
'Non-Market Rent' — affordable, subsidized, Section 8, HUD, LIHTC, Housing Choice Voucher, PHA, tax-credit, rent-controlled, deed-restricted/inclusionary, or income-restricted housing
'Short Term Rental (STR)' — vacation rentals, Airbnb/VRBO-style operations, or units rented for under 30 days
'Single Room Occupancy (SRO)' — SRO buildings, rooming/boarding houses, or units with shared kitchens/bathrooms
'Market Rate' — privately owned or unrestricted-rental residential use (condominium, apartments, single-family, conventional multifamily) with no income-restriction, subsidy, or program indicators present in the Named Insured, DBA, occupancy description, or unit-level rent data
'Not Applicable' — non-residential properties (commercial, industrial, vacant land, parking) or any case where the housing type is unclear or ambiguous in the source
Classify only from explicit evidence in the source (property name, description, occupancy field, or stated use); do not infer from location or building size alone, and do not default to any value in the absence of such evidence.
The property tenant screening type ID.
Property occupancy sub-type per definitions API
Assisted living operator type for the property (Owner, ThirdParty, or null)
Year the property was built (0/null for vacant land; max 2100)
Property building value in USD/$ (min 0)
Property annual rental income in USD (min 0)
Number of buildings on the property (0/null for vacant land). This is a count for the row, not an identifier — do not confuse it with Building Number.
Number of stories/floors of the property (0/null for vacant land)
Property industrial square footage (min 0)
Property retail square footage (min 0)
Property residential square footage (min 0)

Number of residential units or condos in the property (min 0). Add both residential and commercial units if found in the same address. Read it from the document's unit column even when labeled differently, e.g. 'Number of Units', '# of Units', '# Units', 'Units', 'No. of Units', 'Unit Count'. Do not leave blank when a unit count is present in the document.
Property Total Insurable Value (TIV) of the building, if available.
Property total square footage (min 0)
Whether the property has a mansard roof (true/false)
Whether there is equipment on the property's roof (true/false)
Whether the property uses the primary limit (true/false)

data_validation_rules: Every entry must carry the field values read from its own source row. Never return an entry whose fields are all blank.

Output cardinality equals the number of source data rows. Location Number, Building Number, Location Name, and Street Address 1 are not identity keys and not unique; never use them to group, dedupe, merge, or count entries.
Adding Location Number and Building Number must not reduce coverage. If the entry count is at or near the number of distinct locations rather than the number of rows, the extraction is wrong.
No property row is optional. Extract rows with blank identifiers, blank addresses, zero units, or zero values.
